papers.title: Rigidity for Families of Abelian Varieties over $\mathcal{M}_{g,n}$
papers.abstract: We provide a new proof of Farb's theorem on the global rigidity of the period map $\mathcal{M}_{g,n} \to \mathcal{A}_g$. We extend this classification to essentially include the period map for $\mathcal{M}_{2,n}$. We also provide a classification of holomorphic maps $\mathcal{M}_g \to \mathcal{A}_{h}$ for $h \leq 2g-1$. The only nonconstant maps in this range are given by taking the Jacobian of a curve and attaching a fixed Abelian variety. In addition to the group theory of the mapping class group, we make extensive use of the theory of variations of Hodge structures and the birational geometry on $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_2$.

papers.title: The $k$-th Milnor and Tjurina numbers: conjectures and a bifurcation formula for pairs
papers.abstract: We study the higher-order Milnor and Tjurina numbers of isolated hypersurface singularities and extend these invariants to pairs of plane holomorphic germs. We first show that a conjectured upper bound of Hussain, Yau and Zuo on the ratio between the higher-order Milnor and Tjurina numbers of isolated hypersurface singularities in three-dimensional complex space does not hold: it fails already for the simplest singularity, a non-degenerate quadratic one, and the ratio tends to infinity as the order grows. We then prove that a conjecture of Shi, Yau and Zuo on semiquasihomogeneous singularities holds for plane curves, for every order and over formal power series, and show that it fails in dimension three. Using the theory of higher-order Milnor and Tjurina numbers of foliations in dimension two, we introduce these invariants for pairs of plane germs. For every order, we show that the higher-order Milnor number of a pair is determined by the Milnor number of the pair and the algebraic multiplicity of the associated foliation, and we compute the difference between the higher-order Milnor and Tjurina numbers of the pair. Finally, we establish a bifurcation formula comparing the higher-order Milnor number of a pair with that of the product of the germs. As a consequence, we characterize semitame meromorphic germs as those for which these two numbers agree at some order, or equivalently at every order.

papers.title: Sharp condition for the existence of wave operators
papers.abstract: We study the wave operators for a Jacobi matrix whose spectral measure satisfies the Szeg\H{o} condition. We formulate a sufficient condition in terms of the associated Verblunsky parameters and show that it is sharp.

papers.title: Radial symmetry for the positive K\"ahler--Einstein Dirichlet problem on the ball
papers.abstract: We prove radial symmetry for every strictly plurisubharmonic function $u$ on the unit ball in $\C^n$, $n\ge2$, that is smooth up to the boundary, vanishes there, and has complex Hessian determinant $\mu e^{-u}$ for a constant $\mu>0$. The known Fubini--Study family therefore exhausts all such solutions. For the corresponding complex Monge--Amp\`ere mean field equation, this establishes the Berman--Berndtsson symmetry conjecture in the smooth class and gives uniqueness throughout the known existence range. The classification also yields the sharp Moser--Trudinger inequality on the ball in Cegrell's finite-energy class.

papers.title: Toeplitz coefficients and the Lu-Tian correspondence on Sasakian manifolds
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a compact embeddable strictly pseudoconvex CR manifold with Reeb field $T$ and Szeg\H o projection $\Pi$. Herrmann, Hsiao, Marinescu and the second author showed, for any volume form, that the semi-classical cut-offs $\chi(k^{-1}\Pi P\Pi)$ of first-order elliptic self-adjoint Toeplitz operators have full asymptotic expansions. For $P=-\sqrt{-1}T$ and $T$-invariant volume forms, Chang, Herrmann and Hsiao showed that the diagonal coefficients are $a_{j}\int\chi(t)t^{n-j}dt$ with local invariants $a_{j}$, computed $a_{0}$ and $a_{1}$, and used normal forms in the Sasakian case. We add one step: on a compact Sasakian manifold, regular or not, $a_{j}=a_{j}(g^{T})/(2\pi^{n+1})$, where $a_{j}(\cdot)$ is the universal Bergman kernel polynomial and $g^{T}$ the transverse K\"ahler metric; no line bundle on $X$ is needed. This gives an exact correspondence: the logarithmic term of the Szeg\H o kernel vanishes to infinite order over an open set if and only if $a_{j}(g^{T})=0$ there for all $j\ge n+1$, which for circle bundles is a local form of the theorem of Lu and Tian with its converse. For $(n,0)$-forms on complete Sasakian manifolds, a cut-off by the self-adjoint generator of the Reeb flow, which avoids the self-adjointness question for the Toeplitz operator, gives the same results with twisted coefficients.

papers.title: Singular sets of conformal curves are discrete
papers.abstract: We prove that the differential of a non-constant conformal curve between Euclidean spaces has full rank outside a discrete set. In particular, conformal curves are real-analytic outside a discrete set. We provide examples of entire associative and coassociative conformal curves with a non-empty singular set. We show that every non-constant Special Lagrangian conformal curve is a real-analytic conformal immersion. We also prove that a non-constant conformal curve has discrete fibers.

papers.title: Complete solutions and subharmonic functions
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a Riemann surface, $K_X \rightarrow X$ the canonical bundle, and $T_X\coloneqq K_X^{-1}\rightarrow X$ the dual bundle of the canonical bundle. For each integer $r \geq 2$, each $q \in H^0(K_X^r)$, and each choice of the square root $K_X^{1/2}$ of the canonical bundle, we canonically obtain a Higgs bundle $(\K_r,\Phi(q))\rightarrow X$, which is called a cyclic Higgs bundle. A diagonal solution $h = (h_1, \dots, h_r)$ to the Hitchin equation on a cyclic Higgs bundle yields $r-1$ Hermitian metrics $H_1, \dots, H_{r-1}$ on $T_X\rightarrow X$, defined as $H_j \coloneqq h_j^{-1} \otimes h_{j+1}$ for each $j=1,\dots, r-1$, while $h_1$, $h_r$, and $q$ yield a Hermitian metric $H_r$ on $T_X \rightarrow X$ which is degenerate at the zero set of $q$. A diagonal solution is said to be complete if the K\"ahler metrics induced by $H_1,\dots, H_{r-1}$ are all complete. Li--Mochizuki established a theorem stating that, for any Riemann surface $X$ and any $q$ that is non-zero unless $X$ is hyperbolic, there exists a unique complete solution $h$ to the Hitchin equation for the cyclic Higgs bundle $(\K_r,\Phi(q))$ with $\det(h)=1$. The holomorphic section $q$ induces a subharmonic weight function $\phi_q=\frac{1}{r}\log|q|^2$ on $K_X\rightarrow X$, and the Hitchin equation depends on $q$ only through this weight function. In previous work, the author introduced a variant of the Hitchin equation associated with an arbitrary subharmonic weight function $\varphi$. In this paper, we extend the Li--Mochizuki theorem to complete solutions of the extended Hitchin equation associated to any subharmonic weight function $\varphi$ that is not identically $-\infty$ unless $X$ is hyperbolic.

papers.title: History independence and base-dominant rigidity for polynomial skew products
papers.abstract: We study history independence of fast directions and its relation to the Binder--DeMarco dimension formula for regular polynomial skew products of degree $d\ge2$. Assuming uniform expansion on the support of the measure of maximal entropy and a base Lyapunov exponent larger than the vertical exponent, we prove that history independence is equivalent to conjugacy to a polynomial product by an affine shear map. Under history independence, the measure of maximal entropy satisfies the Binder--DeMarco dimension formula. If, in addition, the splitting is dominated, the dimension formula also implies history independence. The proof first upgrades the measurable fast direction to a holomorphic line field and then uses its invariance on periodic fibers to force the affine product structure. The converse dimension implication combines an entropy comparison argument with rigidity of local symmetries of periodic fiber Julia sets.

papers.title: On the extension of meromorphic mappings and correspondences with finite volume
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a compact complex manifold. Using Bishop's extension theorem, we show that a meromorphic map, or more generally a meromorphic correspondence, $f\colon\Delta^k_*\to X$ extends meromorphically across $0$ if and only if its graph has finite $2k$-dimensional volume near $\{0\}\times X$; equivalently, all mixed integrals $\int\omega_E^{k-m}\wedge(f^*\omega)^m$, $1\le m\le k$, are finite. The criterion extends to arbitrary proper analytic subsets, and yields an energy criterion with a sharp exponent, a dichotomy for maps into Hopf manifolds, a rationality criterion for maps between projective manifolds, and, for $k=2$ and pluriclosed targets, the equivalence of extension with finiteness of the single integral $\int(f^*\omega)^2$.

papers.title: A proof of Schmeisser's conjecture
papers.abstract: In 1977, Schmeisser proposed a strengthening of Sendov's conjecture: if all zeros of a polynomial $p$ of degree $n\ge2$ lie in the closed unit disk, then for every point $\xi$ in the convex hull of the zeros of $p$, there exists a critical point $\zeta$ of $p$ such that $ |\xi-\zeta|\le 1.$ We prove this conjecture in every degree. The proof combines a covering of the convex hull by diameter disks, inequalities for reflected polynomials, and quantitative estimates for centred products, supplemented by rigorous computer-assisted verification in a finite range of degrees.

papers.title: Multidimensional mixed Bohr radii for Banach space valued holomorphic functions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce and study a generalized notion of multidimensional mixed Bohr radii for holomorphic functions defined on the unit ball of the finite-dimensional Minkowski sequence space with values in complex Banach spaces. We first prove that the multidimensional mixed Bohr radius is positive for every non-null bounded linear operator whose norm is sufficiently small relative to the scaling parameter. We then determine the exact asymptotic behavior of the multidimensional mixed Bohr radius for infinite-dimensional Banach spaces of finite cotype and we obtain analogous bounds for spaces without finite cotype. Finally, for concave Banach lattices and summing operators, we prove lower bounds that involve a logarithmic factor. These results connect classical scalar Bohr phenomena with operator-valued and Banach space valued settings, and highlight how the geometry of the spaces and the mapping properties of the operator influence coefficient estimates and their dependence on dimension. Several examples illustrate the consistency of our results with the classical Bohr radius and the sharp Defant--Frerick asymptotics.

papers.title: Strictly pseudoconvex $CR$ structures on $\sfS^5$ that can be turned inside out
papers.abstract: The existence of a complex structure on $\sfS^{6}$ implies that of strictlty pseudoconvex structures on $\sfS^{5}$ which can be turned inside out by a homotopy.

papers.title: Weighted composition operators between Qp spaces: Boundedness and compactness
papers.abstract: We characterize boundedness and compactness of weighted composition operators $W_{u,\varphi}:Q_{p_1}\to Q_{p_2}$, where $W_{u,\varphi}f=u(f\circ\varphi)$, $p_1>0$, and $0<p_2<1$. A separation theorem for the two terms in $(W_{u,\varphi}f)'$, together with value and derivative embedding theorems, gives two capacity conditions on $u$ and $\varphi$. For $p_1=1$ and $p_1>1$, the derivative condition has a maximal-integral and an area-integral form respectively.

papers.title: Hausdorff continuity of logarithmic and Riesz capacities
papers.abstract: Let $E_n$ be $\alpha_n$-uniformly perfect compact sets that converge to a compact set $E$ in the Hausdorff distance $d_n=d_H(E_n,E)$. We prove that the logarithmic capacity of $E_n$ converges to that of $E$ whenever $\log(1/\alpha_n)=O(\log(1/d_n))$ and that no factor tending to infinity can be inserted in this bound. A common energy-transfer theorem also yields Hausdorff continuity of Riesz capacity under local capacity bounds, including bounds obtained from lower Hausdorff content density. Finally, we correct our earlier claims about the uniform convergence of Green functions.

papers.title: Uniform compactness in a family of $\bar{\partial}$-Neumann problems
papers.abstract: In their paper on non-coercive boundary value problems, Kohn and Nirenberg show that a priori estimates for all forms satisfying $\bar{\partial}$-Neumann boundary conditions follow from a compactness estimate. Inspired by Hamilton, we show that these a priori estimates are stable under deformations of the complex structure, the hermitian metric and the volume form of the underlying manifold. We use a parameter $m$ to encode a deformation of this data. We show that if a family of $\bar{\partial}$-Neumann problems depends smoothly on $m$ and the compactness estimate(s) hold (with constants uniform in $m$), then the family of solution operators also depends smoothly $m$. As a consequence we obtain sufficient conditions for the Bergman kernel to vary smoothly in a family of domains. We also provide a sufficient condition for the uniform compactness estimate(s) to hold in a family of domains.

papers.title: A note on meromorphicity in infinite dimensions
papers.abstract: In this note we develop the notion of a meromorphic mapping between infinite-dimensional complex manifolds. We restrict ourselves with second countable Hilbert manifolds modelled on a separable Hilbert space.

papers.title: On the Starshapedness of the Symmetrized Bidisc
papers.abstract: It is well known that the symmetrized bidisc $\mathbb{G}_2$ is star-like about the point $(0,0)$. In our attempt to check if there are other points about which $\mathbb{G}_2$ is star-like, we find that $\mathbb{G}_2$ cannot be starlike about any point $(s,p)\neq(0,0)\in \mathbb{G}_2$.

papers.title: On strongly pseudoconvex K\"ahler--Berwald manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish the equivalence between the K\"ahler--Finsler and K\"ahler--Berwald conditions for complex Finsler metrics. That is, a K\"ahler--Finsler metric always satisfies the complex Berwald condition: its Chern--Finsler nonlinear connection reduces to the Chern connection of a K\"ahler metric. We also provide, for the first time, smooth weakly K\"ahler--Finsler examples which are not K\"ahler--Berwald; and propose a condition that is formally stronger than weakly K\"ahler--Finsler, with equivalence holding in complex dimension two. Then we prove the de Rham decomposition and uniformization theorems for K\"ahler--Berwald manifolds, and show that every strongly pseudoconvex locally symmetric complex Finsler metric is both K\"ahler--Berwald and complex Einstein--Finsler. Additionally, we establish several rigidity theorems for the Kobayashi and Carath\'eodory metrics: $F_K$ is K\"ahler--Berwald if and only if it is K\"ahler; if the manifold is simply connected, then $F_C$ is K\"ahler--Berwald if and only if it is K\"ahler.

papers.title: Domino tilings of black-and-white Temperleyan cylinders
papers.abstract: We consider the dimer model in cylindrical domains $\Omega_\delta$ on square grids of mesh size $\delta$ with two Temperleyan boundary components of different colors. Assuming that the $\Omega_\delta$ approximate a cylindrical domain $\Omega$ as $\delta\to 0$, we prove the convergence of height fluctuations to the Gaussian Free Field in $\Omega$ plus an independent discrete Gaussian multiple of the harmonic measure of one of the boundary components. The limit of the dimer coupling functions on $\Omega_\delta$ is holomorphic in $\Omega$ but not conformally covariant. Given this, we determine the limiting structure of height fluctuations from general principles rather than from explicit computations. In particular, our analysis justifies the inevitable appearance of the discrete Gaussian distribution in the doubly connected setup.

papers.title: On the Milnor classes of local complete intersections
papers.abstract: In this work we study algebraic, geometric and topological properties of the Milnor classes of local complete intersections with arbitrary singularities. We describe first the Milnor class of the intersection of a finite number of hypersurfaces, under certain conditions of transversality, in terms of the Milnor classes of the hypersurfaces. Using this description we obtain a Parusi\'{n}ski-Pragacz type formula, an Aluffi type formula and a description of the Milnor class of the local complete intersection in terms of the global L\^e cycles of the hypersurfaces that define it. We consider next the general case of a local complete intersection $Z(s)$ defined by a regular section $s$ of a rank $r$ holomorphic bundle $E$ over a compact manifold $M$, $r \geq 2$. We notice that $s$ determines a hypersurface $Z(\tilde s)$ in the total space of the projectivization $\mathbb{P}(E^{\vee})$ of the dual bundle $E^{\vee}$, and we give a formula expressing the total Milnor class of the local complete intersection $Z(s)$ in terms of the Milnor classes of the hypersurface $Z(\tilde s)$.

papers.title: On Pseudo-Effectivity and Volumes of Adjoint Classes in K\"ahler Families with Projective Central Fiber
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to studying the deformation behavior of pseudo-effective canonical divisors and volumes of adjoint classes in K\"ahler families. Based on recent developments in the K\"ahler minimal model program, for flat families with fiberwise canonical singularities, we establish the global stability of the pseudo-effectivity of canonical divisors and uniruledness, assuming in addition that one fiber is projective, while the same conclusion for K\"ahler threefolds is also true without the projectivity assumption of the central fiber. For a smooth K\"ahler family whose central fiber is projective with a big adjoint class, we show that its volume remains locally constant. Finally, using the (relative) minimal model program for K\"ahler threefolds, we verify the deformation invariance of volumes of adjoint classes and plurigenera for smooth K\"ahler families of threefolds, thereby partially confirming Siu's invariance of plurigenera conjecture in dimension three.

papers.title: On Milnor and Tjurina numbers of Pairs of Holomorphic Function Germs
papers.abstract: Motivated by the bifurcation formula for the Milnor number of pairs of holomorphic function germs, we introduce, via foliation theory, the Tjurina number of such pairs. We define it as the generic value of the Tjurina number of the foliation associated with the pair, with respect to a specified family of balanced divisors of separatrices. We prove that this value is well defined and that it is an analytic invariant, we derive an explicit formula for it, and we establish a bifurcation formula. As an application, we characterize semitame pairs in terms of this invariant. We also prove a version of Teissier's lemma for pairs and an upper bound for the Milnor number of a pair, and we apply these results to generic pencils of algebraic curves.

papers.title: Chern bounds and tangent geometry of polarized Calabi-Yau threefolds
papers.abstract: We study the numerical geography and tangent geometry of very amply polarized Calabi-Yau threefolds $(X,H)$ through the positivity of the first jet bundle $J^1(H)$. Let $d=\int_X H^3$, $c=\int_Xc_2(X) H$, and $e=\int_X c_3(X)$. We obtain $e\ge-5d-c-c^2/(4d)$ by mixed intersections on $\mathbb{P}(J^1(H)^*)$, and $e\ge40d\left[(1-\frac{c}{10d})^{3/2}-1\right]$ by a volume estimate for a perturbed tautological class. In particular, the latter inequality shows $e+6c\ge0$, improving Sun's inequality $e+10c\ge0$. As consequences, we show (1) the uniform Hodge bounds $-4d-80\le h^{1,1}(X)-h^{2,1}(X)\le173d/66$, (2) the lower bound $\mathrm{deg} X^\vee\ge78$ for the dual hypersurface, and (3) the upper bound $d\le34$ in the critical case $X\subset\mathbb{P}^6$.

papers.title: Complete harmonic metrics and subharmonic functions on the unit disc
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a Riemann surface with canonical bundle $K_X$ and holomorphic tangent bundle $T_X=K_X^{-1}$. For each integer $r\geq 2$, each $q\in H^0(K_X^r)$, and each choice of a square root of $K_X$, we obtain a cyclic Higgs bundle. A diagonal harmonic metric $h=(h_1,\ldots,h_r)$ induces Hermitian metrics $H_j=h_j^{-1}\otimes h_{j+1}$ on $T_X$ for $j=1,\ldots,r-1$, together with a possibly degenerate Hermitian metric $H_r$ determined by $h_1,h_r$, and $q$. We call $h$ complete if the K\"ahler metrics induced by $H_1,\ldots,H_{r-1}$ are all complete. Li--Mochizuki proved that if $q$ is nonzero unless $X$ is hyperbolic, there exists a unique complete harmonic metric on the corresponding cyclic Higgs bundle satisfying $\det(h)=1$. The Hitchin equation depends on $q$ only through the subharmonic weight $\phi_q=\frac{1}{r}\log|q|^2$ on $K_X$. We establish uniqueness of complete solutions with determinant $1$ for general subharmonic weight functions $\varphi$ whose exponentials are $C^2$ outside a compact subset of $X$. On the unit disc $\mathbb D=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|<1\}$, we also prove that a real complete solution exists for every subharmonic weight function. We further establish a monotone approximation theorem. If $\varphi_\epsilon$ are smooth subharmonic weight functions on the discs $\mathbb D_\epsilon=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|<1-\epsilon\}$ decreasing to $\varphi$ as $\epsilon\searrow0$, the corresponding complete solutions $h_\epsilon$, normalized by $\det(h_\epsilon)=1$, converge monotonically to a complete solution $h$ associated with $\varphi$.

papers.title: Absolutely Summing Toeplitz operators on Fock spaces
papers.abstract: For $1\le p<\infty$, let $F^p_\varphi$ be the Fock spaces on ${\mathbb C}^n$ with the weight function $\varphi$ that \(\varphi \in {\mathcal{C}}^{2}\left( {\mathbb{C}}^{n}\right)\) is real-valued and satisfies $ m{\omega }_{0} \leq d{d}^{c}\varphi \leq M{\omega }_{0} $ for two positive constants \(m\) and \(M\), \({\omega }_{0} = d{d}^{c}{\left| z\right| }^{2}\) is the Euclidean K\"{a}hler form on \({\mathbb{C}}^{n}\), \({d}^{c} = \frac{\sqrt{-1}}{4}\left( {\bar{\partial } - \partial }\right)\). In this paper, we completely characterize those positive Borel measure $\mu$ on ${\mathbb C}^n$ so that the induced Toeplitz operators $T_\mu$ is $r$-summing on $F_{\varphi}^{p}$ for $r \ge 1$.

papers.title: Automorphisms of the Worm Domain
papers.abstract: The Diederich--Forn\ae ss worm domain, an important example of a smoothly bounded pseudoconvex domain without a Stein neighborhood basis, provides key counterexamples in the theory of several complex variables. In this paper, we examine its automorphism group and observe that its boundary is locally spherical everywhere except at the exceptional locus and the closure of the caps.

papers.title: Log canonical thresholds at infinity
papers.abstract: The paper considers a global version of the notion of log canonical threshold for plurisubharmonic functions $u$ of logarithmic growth in $\mathbb{C}^n$, aiming at description of the range of all $p>0$ such that $e^{-u}\in L^p(\mathbb{C}^n)$. Explicit formulas are obtained in the toric case. By considering Bergman functions of corresponding weighted Hilbert spaces, a new polynomial approximation of plurisubharmonic functions of logarithmic growth with control over its singularities and behavior at infinity (a global version of Demailly's approximation theorem) is established. Some application to tame polynomial maps are given.

papers.title: Uniform Airy expansions for Ramanujan's function and the Stieltjes--Wigert edge kernel
papers.abstract: For $q=e^{-\varepsilon}\to1^-$, we obtain an Airy expansion for Ramanujan's entire function $A_q(\sqrt q\,x)$, uniformly for $x$ in a sufficiently small fixed complex neighborhood of $1/4$. After an explicit exponential normalization, the expansion has analytic coefficients and a nonlinear Airy argument. We calculate the first corrections and bound the remainder by $\varepsilon^2$ times an Airy envelope. The estimate is valid at Airy zeros and retains exponential decay on the real interval below $1/4$. The proof uses a Gaussian integral representation and an odd analytic change of variable that reduces the phase to cubic form. The compact turning-point expansion follows as a corollary. For each fixed positive zero $\rho_n(q)$, we obtain an expansion of $\log(4\rho_n(q))$ through order $\varepsilon^2$, with remainder $O_n(\varepsilon^{8/3})$. A zero-free interval identifies the zeros by their global indices. We also calculate the $\varepsilon^{2/3}$ correction to the known Airy limit of the Stieltjes--Wigert edge kernel, with an $O(\varepsilon^{4/3})$ remainder uniformly on compact sets, including the diagonal.

papers.title: Uniform Green packing and quantitative transversality on compact Riemann surfaces
papers.abstract: We extend the packing results of Etayo, Hedenmalm, and Ortega-Cerda for complex tori to arbitrary compact Riemann surfaces. The construction uses two different approaches, one based on complex geometry of line bundles, and the other on spetral designs. Both approaches give the same basic existence of close-to-optimal point configurations on the given surface. This version was written with some assistance from ChatGPT.

papers.title: Exponential Green energies, quantization, and minimizers on compact Riemann surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the exponential Green energies associated with a finite point configuration on a Riemann surface. We focus on studying optimal or close-to-optimal configurations, and show that they must be well-spread out on the surface. We study in particular the round sphere and obtain values for the minimal Green energy of a configuration. The first version of this paper was written with some assistance from ChatGPT.
